Attention weights over transmitted moments

Source: R/attention.R
attention_weights.Rd

Scores each transmitted moment against a query moment and turns the scores into weights. The key of record \(h\) is the projector \(P_h\) onto its leading k eigenvectors. With score = "energy" the score is \(s_h = tr(P_h R_0)\), where \(R_0\) is the energy-normalised moment of the query; when \(R_0\) is the full moment of a set of beats, \(1 - s_h\) is their mean per-beat relative error in the basis of record \(h\). With score = "projection" the score is \(tr(P_h P_0)/k\), symmetric in the two subspaces, where \(P_0\) projects onto the leading k eigenvectors of \(R_0\). With score = "cosine" it is the cosine between \(R_0\) and \(M_h\) in the Frobenius inner product. The scores depend on the eigenvectors only through \(P_h\) or \(M_h\), and are therefore unchanged by their signs, order or any rotation within the retained subspace.

Usage

attention_weights(
  query,
  moments,
  k,
  tau,
  top = NULL,
  score = "energy",
  normalize = "softmax",
  sink = NULL
)

Arguments

query

A bp_moment object, a \(p \times p\) moment matrix or a beat matrix, from which a full-rank energy moment is computed.

moments

A list of bp_moment objects.

k

Dimension of the keys.

tau

Temperature. Inf gives equal weights and 0 puts all weight on the highest score, shared among ties.

top

Optional number of largest weights kept, the others set to zero and the kept ones renormalised. A compressor then transmits top indices and weights instead of one weight per record.

score

One of "energy", "projection" or "cosine".

normalize

"softmax", or "sparsemax", the Euclidean projection of \(s/\tau\) onto the simplex, which sets low scores to zero.

sink

Optional offset of an extra key, the mean of the transmitted moments, whose score is its own score plus sink. Its weight, in the attribute sink, goes to the population moment.

Value

A vector of weights over the records, with the scores in the attribute scores, the weight of the extra key in sink and the effective number of records \(1 / \sum_h w_h^2\) in n_eff.

Examples

sim <- simulate_beats(H = 5, n = 60, p = 20, q = 3, seed = 4)
m <- lapply(sim$X, energy_moment, q = 5)
attention_weights(sim$X[[1]][1:20, ], m[-1], k = 3, tau = 0.01)
#> [1] 0.1374985 0.1566100 0.1343125 0.5715790
#> attr(,"scores")
#> [1] 0.6172103 0.6185117 0.6169759 0.6314582
#> attr(,"sink")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"n_eff")
#> [1] 2.576158
